notes.meaning: The LORD declares that heaven is his throne and the earth is merely a rest for his feet. He asks what kind of house humans could ever build that would be great enough to contain him or serve as his resting place. God is far too immense to be confined to any earthly building. We must remember his supreme majesty whenever we come to worship him.

God reminds his people that his own hands created everything in the universe, so he has no need of human gifts. What he truly values is not a grand temple, but a humble person who is deeply grieved over sin. The Lord looks with favor on anyone who trembles with reverent awe at his word. Our inner attitude of heart matters far more to God than outward religious displays.

The Lord compares the sacrifices of unrepentant people to horrible sins. Offering an ox or incense while living in rebellion is as vile to him as murder, killing an unclean dog, offering pig's blood, or praising a false idol. Religious rituals mean nothing to God when the worshippers take pleasure in wicked ways. Outward worship without an obedient heart is completely detestable to the Lord.

Because the people chose their own wicked paths, God promises to bring upon them the very calamities and terrors they tried to escape. He called out to them repeatedly through his prophets, but no one answered or paid attention. They deliberately chose evil in his sight, so he chooses their punishment. Refusing to listen to God always leads to painful consequences.

The Lord speaks words of comfort to the faithful few who revere his word. Their own countrymen hated them, threw them out of fellowship, and sarcastically mocked their hope that God would be glorified. But the Lord promises to appear and fill the faithful with joy, while their persecutors will be put to open shame. God never forgets his followers when they suffer rejection for his sake.

A sudden, terrifying sound of tumult breaks out from the city and the temple. This is the mighty voice of the Lord himself executing justice and paying back his enemies what they deserve. Those who trusted in an empty building while living in rebellion will not escape his judgment. God's justice is certain and cannot be avoided.

Zion is described as giving birth to a son suddenly and without the usual labor pains. This picture shows how swiftly and easily God can bring about the deliverance and renewal of his people. What seems impossible to human strength is accomplished by the Lord in an instant. God can turn our seasons of waiting into sudden breakthroughs of life and blessing.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Some Catholic teachers see this verse as a prophetic sign of Mary giving birth to Jesus without physical labor pains.

notes.meaning: The prophet expresses amazement at how an entire country or nation could be born in a single day. Yet as soon as Zion entered labor, she brought forth her children all at once. This looked forward to the rapid return of the exiles and the sudden expansion of God's church under the preaching of the gospel. God's saving power works on a scale far beyond human understanding.

differ.view: Some Baptists emphasize from this verse that the church must experience deep spiritual travail and earnest prayer before souls can be born again.

notes.meaning: The Lord asks whether he would bring a child all the way to the point of delivery and then fail to give birth. He reassures his people that he who opens the womb will never close it prematurely or abandon his plan. God never leaves his promises half-finished. We can be completely confident that the Lord will carry through whatever good work he begins.

Everyone who truly loves Jerusalem and has grieved over her past ruins is invited to celebrate with her. God calls those who shared in her sorrows to enter fully into her newfound gladness. When God restores his people, he invites all who care for his work to share in the feast. Faithful sorrow over the trials of God's people leads to lasting joy.

The restored city is pictured as a loving mother who nurses her children with rich comfort and abundant nourishment. Believers will feast upon the spiritual blessings, peace, and promises given through God's renewed people. God provides more than enough grace to satisfy the longings of our souls. We find true spiritual satisfaction when we draw near to God's presence.

The Lord promises to direct deep peace to Jerusalem like an overflowing river, along with the wealth and honor of the surrounding nations. God's people will be cared for with gentle tenderness, carried on the side and bounced playfully on the knees like favored children. God supplies both boundless peace and warm, motherly care for his family. We can rest safely in the gentle affection of our Lord.

The Lord compares his own comforting presence to the gentle, soothing love of a mother caring for her child. In Jerusalem, his people will discover genuine relief from their long griefs and painful memories. God's tenderness is deep enough to reach the deepest wounds of the human heart. No earthly comfort compares to the gentle compassion God pours out on his children.

When God's people see this marvelous restoration, their hearts will rejoice and their weary bodies will flourish with new strength like green grass. The Lord will openly reveal his helping hand to his loyal servants while pouring out his indignation against his enemies. God shows great mercy to those who trust him and strict justice to those who oppose him. The joy of the Lord restores our deepest strength.

The Lord is pictured arriving in judgment with flaming fire and war chariots as swift and crushing as a whirlwind. He comes to execute his righteous fury and rebuke his persistent enemies with burning flames. God's holy hatred of sin will burn away all ungodly rebellion. We must remember that our holy God is a consuming fire against evil.

The Lord will hold court and carry out his sentence against all ungodly people by fire and by his sword, leaving many slain. The fire points to devastating divine judgments, while the sword points to warfare and the conflicts of history. When God finally rises to judge the earth, no stubborn sinner will be able to stand. God's righteous verdict is final and irresistible.

The Lord pronounces destruction upon those who perform pagan rituals in secret gardens while following false leaders into forbidden practices. These hypocrites pretended to purify themselves but blatantly broke God's law by eating pigs, mice, and other detestable creatures. Secret sin and religious pretense will be completely wiped out by God's judgment. God sees right through empty ritual to our secret motives and actions.

God sees the hidden thoughts and corrupt works of all people, and he announces that he is coming to gather every nation and tongue. When they assemble, they will behold his glorious majesty and divine power. God's plans are not confined to a single group of people, but encompass all humanity. The whole world will ultimately recognize the supreme glory of the living God.

The Lord promises to set up a sign among the people and send spared survivors to distant Gentile nations that had never heard his name. These messengers will travel to distant places—such as Tarshish, Put, Lud, Tubal, and the Greek islands—to declare his glory to foreigners. God uses those he has redeemed to spread his fame across the ends of the earth. We are called to share God's wonderful salvation with those who have never heard.

The nations will bring God's scattered people back to Jerusalem as an offering to the Lord, using horses, chariots, wagons, mules, and camels. They will treat these returning believers with great care and reverence, just as worshippers carry clean offerings to the temple. God moves the hearts of outsiders to help gather his chosen family into his house. God faithfully brings his people home from every far corner of the earth.

The Lord promises that he will choose some of these newly gathered people to serve as priests and Levites (temple ministers). In the new era of the gospel, sacred ministry is no longer limited to one Jewish tribe, but is opened to people from all nations who turn to God. God elevates former outsiders to the highest honors of spiritual service. The Lord welcomes all believers into intimate access and holy service before him.

Just as the new heavens and the new earth that God creates will endure before him forever, so the name and descendants of his faithful people will never pass away. God's redeemed family is granted an everlasting existence that cannot be destroyed by time or earthly change. His covenant promises are as permanent as the eternal universe he makes. Believers can rest secure in the knowledge that their future is forever safe with God.

The Lord envisions a day when all humanity will gather regularly to worship before him, month after month and week after week. While Old Testament festivals like New Moons and Sabbaths are used to describe the scene, the passage points to steady, joyful worship from every corner of the earth. True worship will become the constant delight of all nations. God's great purpose is to receive loving worship from all mankind.

As worshippers depart from God's presence, they will look upon the rotting bodies of those who rebelled against him. The prophet pictures their terrible end with worms that never die and a fire that is never put out, making them an object of horror to all. Jesus later used these very words to warn of the eternal reality of hell and the awful cost of rejecting God. Seeing the terrible end of rebellion should make us deeply thankful for God's saving grace.

differ.view: Some evangelicals believe this verse describes conditional immortality, where the unquenchable fire completely consumes the wicked until they cease to exist.
